input.title: agentHost: map legacy `chat.tools.eligibleForAutoApproval` to managed settings
input.body:
## What

Adds a **temporary compatibility mapping** for the legacy VS Code setting `chat.tools.eligibleForAutoApproval` (enterprise policy `ChatToolsEligibleForAutoApproval`) to the Copilot SDK managed-settings bridge in [`agentHostManagedSettings.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostManagedSettings.ts). Like the other four legacy mappings, it is gated behind the existing false-by-default `chat.agentHost.copilot.mapLegacySettingsToManagedSettings`.

## Why it maps to the bypass lock rather than per-tool `ask` rules

The setting is **per-tool** (`{ "fetch": false, "runTask": false }` → those tools may never be auto-approved). The SDK managed rule grammar has **no tool-name family** — `ManagedRuleFamily` is only `Shell | Read | Write | Domain`, and an unknown family rejects the *entire* managed document. So a faithful per-tool `ask` rule cannot be built and would silently miss `runTask`, `runTests`, and every MCP/extension tool.

Any policy-configured, non-empty value therefore maps onto the **family-agnostic** bypass lock `{ disableBypassPermissionsMode: 'disable' }`. The runtime's `bypass_blocked()` refuses blanket escalation "regardless of how it was requested", and `'disable'` additionally sets `auto_approval_blocked()` — matching this setting's core intent that a tool "will never offer the option to auto-approve."

This is deliberately **coarser** than the setting and errs **more restrictive** (fail-closed), which is the safe direction for an interim shim: it can never silently grant more than the administrator intended.

- `policyOnly` sourcing: only an enterprise `policyValue` drives it — never user/application/workspace — because it removes a capability the user would otherwise have.
- Empty `{}` (the registered default), absent, and malformed (non-object/array) values contribute nothing.
- A non-empty object whose members are malformed (e.g. `{ "fetch": "no" }`) fails **closed** toward the lock rather than being silently dropped.

## Known trade-offs (documented in the module header)

- A permissive value such as `{ "fetch": true }` still disables escalation session-wide (no way to scope to one tool).
- It does not force per-request confirmation — only an `ask` rule sets `managedApprovalRequired`, so a user may still grant a standing approval for an individual tool.
- **Removal criterion:** replace with a faithful per-tool translation once the runtime managed grammar gains a tool-name rule family.

## Scope

- Declares `ELIGIBLE_FOR_AUTO_APPROVAL_SETTING_ID` in [`agentHostSchema.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostSchema.ts) so the platform-layer bridge avoids importing `ChatConfiguration` from workbench (passes `valid-layers-check`).
- Leaves the workbench consumers (`languageModelToolsService.ts`, `terminalToolAutoApprove.ts`) **untouched** so in-workbench chat keeps its per-tool behavior.

## Testing

- `./scripts/test.sh --grep AgentHostManagedSettings` — 26 passing (7 new: configured value, empty `{}`, non-policy layers contribute nothing, removal clears, malformed array ignored, fail-closed non-boolean member, un-duplicated co-existence with a policy-disabled `chat.tools.global.autoApprove`).
- `./scripts/test.sh --grep AgentHostProtocolClient` — 97 passing (no regression).
- `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run valid-layers-check`, and `npm run eslint` all clean.

## Review

Cross-checked by a three-model review council (GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.3-Codex): no blocking issues. The one raised point — a non-boolean object member still locks bypass — is the intended fail-closed behavior; a documenting test and a doc-comment clarification were added in response.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
